info.name: Dispatch Load Balancer API
info.description:
Delivery orders assigned to capacity-limited vehicles: HIGH priority first, then the nearest drop by Haversine distance from each vehicle's current route tip, reported as a round trip.

How to run: start the stack (docker compose up -d, then .\mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run), import this file (Import > File), then run folders 0 to 4 in order. Every assertion is copied from the JUnit suite, so a red request here means a red build too.

Machine-readable contract: {{baseUrl}}/v3/api-docs (importable into Postman directly). Interactive docs: {{baseUrl}}/swagger-ui.html. Full prose reference: API.md in the repo.

item.name: 0 - Setup
item.description: Run this folder first. DELETE /api/dispatch/data is an additive helper (not part of the original spec) that makes the collection repeatable: run it top to bottom twice, the assertions pass identically both times.

item.name: 1 - Delhi demo (645 kg of demand, 500 kg fleet)
item.description: The requirement document's own sample, copied verbatim from src/test/resources/sample/delhi-{vehicles,orders}.json. A perfect plan is impossible by design, so this folder asserts the measured invariant that DispatchPlanE2EIT asserts: 23 orders / 495 kg assigned, exactly 7 LOW orders (150 kg) left unassigned, 171 km of round trips.

request.description: Known-empty start so the plan below is reproducible.
Fleet capacity 500 kg in total.
645 kg total: HIGH 12 orders / 275 kg, MEDIUM 8 / 145 kg, LOW 10 / 225 kg.

item.name: 2 - Bangalore sample (the spec's literal example)
item.description: The exact 2-order / 2-vehicle payload printed in the API specification, and the reason our distances differ from it: the spec's example response says "5 km" and "6 km", which are one-way illustrations, while totalDistance here is the round trip the vehicle actually drives (start -> stop -> start). Hence "10 km" and "8 km" - 2x the spec number, and legs[] shows the arithmetic.

item.name: 3 - Validation and the error matrix
item.description: One request per row of the error contract documented in API.md. Every failure uses the same 7-key envelope (timestamp, status, error, code, message, path, fieldErrors); code is the stable machine-readable field, message is human text. Nothing in this folder inserts a row, so request 39's empty-database case stays valid after 30.

request.description: Folder 3 must run against empty tables.
One request, six field errors: latitude 91, longitude 200, blank orderId, blank address, weight 0 and a missing priority. Note the indexed field paths (orders[0].latitude).
@NotEmpty on the list itself, so the reported field is "orders" rather than an element.

spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties is switched back ON, so a typo'd field is a 400 instead of being silently ignored. It fails at binding, hence MALFORMED_JSON with no fieldErrors.
Unparseable body - the controller is never invoked, so no field information exists.
Enums are resolved by Jackson before bean validation runs, so a bad priority is MALFORMED_JSON, not a field error. Values must be exactly HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW.
The same natural key twice inside one request is ambiguous intent, so it is rejected (D8). Re-posting an existing id across requests is an upsert instead - see folder 4.
Content-Type must be application/json; anything else is refused before parsing.
Only /api/dispatch/data may be deleted. 405, not 404: the path exists but not for this method.
404 only when BOTH tables are empty. Vehicles without orders is a 200 with an empty plan; orders without vehicles is a 200 with every order unassigned (NO_VEHICLES_AVAILABLE).
An unmapped path still gets the same error envelope instead of a framework page.

item.name: 4 - Upsert
item.description: "Efficient database operations (upsert for repository data)" from the evaluation criteria. Re-posting an existing orderId updates the row rather than inserting a second one, and the ack says which happened. The plan then shows ORD001 at 99 kg on VEH001 (capacity 100): the fleet load moves 30 kg -> 119 kg with the same two rows in the table.
